fact: The Rwanda ICT Chamber implements the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship, an 18-month acceleration programme launched in June 2026 for eight Rwandan startups, with US$50,000 each.

TechTrends Africa says Kigali Innovation City, a 61-hectare zone backed by Africa50 and the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa, broke ground in September 2025 and is designed to house startup incubators and accelerators, with Carnegie Mellon Africa already resident.

The Global Fund case study says HealthTech Hub Africa, a pan-African health tech accelerator co-funded by the Global Fund and others, is based in Kigali at Norrsken House, with no startup cohort or programme described.
RISA's Hanga Hubs page says the project established incubation hubs and runs a nine-month cohort programme (ideation, pre-incubation, incubation) for young entrepreneurs, listed as ongoing.
RISA says Hanga Hubs were set up in seven districts: Musanze, Rwamagana, Huye, Muhanga, Nyagatare, Rubavu and Rusizi.

MINICT's page says Kigali Innovation City, a USD 2 billion project in Kigali's Special Economic Zone, is set to host universities, technology companies and startups on 70 hectares, with Africa50 committing USD 400 million.
